header.running_head: Love for Da'wah and Preoccupation with it

blocks.text: Hadhrat Umar (RA) Weeps over the Exertion of a Christian Monk

Abu Imraan Jowni narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by a monk and remained standing there. Someone called the monk and told him that the Ameerul Mu'mineen was there. When the monk peeped out, the effects of difficulty, exertion and forsaking the world were clearly apparent on his face (he had grown extremely pale and haggard on account of his spiritual exertions). Looking at him, Hadhrat Umar (RA) began to weep. "But he is a Christian," someone commented. Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "I know, but I feel sorry for him because I thought of the verse in which Allaah mentions:

He who suffered affliction and who endured many difficulties (thinking that he was pleasing Allaah whereas his beliefs and actions did not conform with the injunctions of Allaah). He shall enter the blazing fire.
I feel sorry for him because despite his exertion and efforts in this world, he shall still end up in Jahannam." [^1]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Invites Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) to Islaam

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that her father Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was a close friend of Rasulullaah ﷺ even during the Period of Ignorance. One day, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) left home to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ. When he met Rasulullaah ﷺ, he said, "O Abul Qaasim[^2]! Why is it that you are no longer present in the gatherings of your people? Why do they accuse you of speaking ill of their forefathers?" Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I am the Rasul of Allaah and am calling you towards Allaah." As soon as Rasulullaah ﷺ had completed, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) accepted Islaam.
When Rasulullaah ﷺ had left Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), there was none between the mountains of Makkah happier than Rasulullaah ﷺ because Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had accepted Islaam. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then met Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA), Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydillaah (RA), Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam (RA) and Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA), all of whom accepted Islaam. The following day, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) met Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA), Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA), Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf (RA), Hadhrat Abu Salma bin Abdil Asad (RA) and Hadhrat Arqam bin Abil Arqam (RA), all of whom also readily
Bayhaqi, Ibn Mundhir and Haakim as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.175).
A title of Rasulullaah ﷺ, meaning father of Qaasim because Rasulullaah ﷺ had a son by the name of Qaasim.
